classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the triangle's perpendicular height from its unequal sloping sides, using the height for end areas and all three side lengths for rectangular faces.

content.prompt: Find the surface area of the triangular prism.

spec.description: Unshaded triangular prism with dimension arrows, a dashed perpendicular altitude, its right-angle marker, and dashed hidden edges. Decorative pale blue face shading is omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: Triangular end: base 21 mm, sides 10 mm and 17 mm, perpendicular height 8 mm. Prism length: 12 mm. The altitude divides the base into 6 mm and 15 mm, consistent with the supplied side lengths; those derived lengths are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements appear; no surface-area answer is printed.

answer.worked:
Front and back triangles:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{triangles}}&=\left(\frac{21\times8}{2}\right)\times2\\A_{\text{triangles}}&=168\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
Side rectangles:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{sides}}&=12\times10+12\times17\\A_{\text{sides}}&=324\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
Bottom rectangle:
$$A_{\text{bottom}}=12\times21=252\text{ mm}^2$$
Total surface area:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{total}}&=168+324+252\\A_{\text{total}}&=744\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
